metadata.title: The AI cloud math is broken, and it’s creating a power shift within Big Tech - MarketWatch

content.text:
Outside the Box
The AI cloud math is broken, and it’s creating a power shift within Big Tech
Buying AI hardware outright is becoming more economical than renting AI power through the cloud
In July, I spent €64,780, or about $75,500, on four artificial-intelligence graphics cards and the server that holds them, rather than renting the same processing power from Amazon.com AMZN by the hour. And if enough companies run that calculation at a much greater scale, it changes who profits from the AI boom.
Let’s look at the math: When it went on sale in April 2025, the Nvidia NVDA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell was initially listed at $8,565. By June 2026, the price jumped up to $13,250. In August 2026, those who wanted the graphics card needed to shell out a staggering $16,000, or roughly 87% above the initial price.
